name: Google Shape;84;p4
text: Smart Devices are not only Software
textPreview: Smart Devices are not only Software

text:
In traditional IT systems we think mainly about software vulnerabilities.
But smart connected devices are different. They include multiple hardware components, secure elements, and third-party modules.
Some vulnerabilities exist in hardware, and many critical assets are managed directly by hardware components.
So without a model that includes hardware, vulnerability management for devices is incomplete.

title: ARIANNA provides support in the creation the Device Model (HBOM + SBOM)

name: Google Shape;99;p5
text:
ARIANNA provides support in the creation the Device Model (HBOM + SBOM)
Device Model is used to identify vulnerabilities in the target device
HBOM: List of hardware components in the target device
Built according to validated hardware part numbers, enriched with info in our internal DB
SBOM: List of software components in the target device
Built according to trusted information retrieved by ARIANNA SCA Tools
ARIANNA Software Composition Analysis Tools 
Scripts (Python, Bash or PowerShell) to be executed in the development environment
SCA Tools output (CSV file) must be uploaded on ARIANNA (through Web UI or Rest APIs)
By elaborating the uploaded CSV, ARIANNA produces the final SBOM
No need to disclose source code
No reverse engineering of binaries
Unprecise SBOM: missing components, or components with wrong version
No agents installed on target devices
Invasive approach, can complicate FW / SW maintenance (agents must be updated during device lifecycle)

name: Google Shape;107;p6
text:

2. Generate CSV evidence for the relevant OS, application, firmware, SDK, or container layers.
3. Upload the CSV outputs through the Web UI or REST API.

5. The updated model immediately drives monitoring, pre-triage, vulnerability review, and reporting.

name: Google Shape;236;p15
text:
CVSS not sufficient for prioritization
CVSS useful to measure the potential risk
Context matters more than Severity Score
A vulnerability in a component that is not exposed to the network is very different from the same vulnerability in an internet-facing device.
Exploitability matters more than quantity
Fixing 50 theoretical vulnerabilities does not improve security as much as fixing 5 vulnerabilities that can really be exploited.

name: Google Shape;237;p15
text: Severity alone is no longer enough
textPreview: Severity alone is no longer enough

text:
Today most vulnerability management processes are based mainly on severity scores like CVSS.
And CVSS is absolutely useful — it gives us a standard way to measure how dangerous a vulnerability could be.

The problem is that severity does not tell us how dangerous a vulnerability is for our specific device.

We are measuring vulnerabilities correctly, but we are prioritizing them incorrectly.

Smart connected devices have different risks than IT systems
Most scoring systems were created for IT environments.
But smart connected devices have firmware, hardware dependencies, and very different attack surfaces.

title: ARIANNA provides a configurable pre-triage engine.

name: Google Shape;243;p16
text:
ARIANNA provides a configurable pre-triage engine.
It splits identified vulnerabilities into two classes:
High Priority: immediate triage required
Low Priority: risk accepted for later management
The goal is to reduce analyst workload while preserving full traceability and human decision-making.

title: Pre-triage does not automatically close or accept vulnerabilities.

name: Google Shape;250;p17
text:
Pre-triage does not automatically close or accept vulnerabilities.
Low-priority vulnerabilities remain visible and traceable for later review.
High-priority vulnerabilities enter analyst triage together with exploitability, reachability, and component context.
The analyst can mark a vulnerability as Not Applicable, Accepted, Mitigated, Fixed, or escalate it for coordinated disclosure.
Every decision is logged and reflected in the report history.
